messages:
sara: prod paging alert — sudden eviction storm + latency cliff on kv-cache in us-east-1. cont-batch write QPS jumped ~4x at 09:12 UTC, paging spikes and lots of `max_batch_tokens`-related timeouts in logs. rolling impact to inference latency, customers reporting 5xx and partial responses.

dev-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0315-001 · Severity P1 · channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall · assigned: miguel (oncall)

oncall-miguel: ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics and current config. https://grafana.example.com/d/kv-cache/us-east-1

ryan: noticed increased tail latency correlated with `cont-batch` batching windows expanding — looks like some clients sent bursts with long seq counts. paging IO skyrocketed.

liz: which config values are live? last deploy changed `max_batch_tokens` to 8192 for perf improvement a week ago.

infra-eli: confirmed: worker-pools in us-east-1 have `max_batch_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=32`, `batch_timeout_ms=200`. KV cache eviction rate shot up 10x — spilling to paging.

oncall-miguel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 2) set `max_num_seqs` to 6 3) bump `batch_timeout_ms` to 100 to force quicker dispatch 4) enable model fallback for heavy routes. rolling now to canary set.

sara: customer impact: we've seen ~3% 5xx across hosted API, and two enterprise customers (acme-corp, sentry-proxy) reported degraded responses. CS pinged them. tagging @customer-success-jamie

customer-success-jamie: emailed both customers with workaround (retry with lower concurrency) and ETA for mitigation. they're watching.

oncall-miguel: running hotfix command:
```
# patch the runtime-config API
curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/configs/us-east-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"cont_batch.max_batch_tokens":1024,"cont_batch.max_num_seqs":6,"cont_batch.batch_timeout_ms":100}'
```

ops-bot: config-patch triggered by miguel at 09:25 UTC. rolling to 10% -> 30% -> 100% (5m ramp).

ryan: metrics after 2m: eviction rate down ~70%, paging IOPS at <30% of peak. tail latency improving but we still see occasional long requests hitting old config due to sticky runtime. continuing.

liz: also enabling temporary per-tenant request-rate limit on heavy route `/v1/generate` to slow the bursters. adding rule for tenants with >500 concurrent streams.

infra-eli: note — GC was disabled in some shards due to prior tuning. re-enabled incremental GC for kv-cache in the hot region as part of the patch.

oncall-miguel: mitigation complete at 09:34 UTC. rolling diag: errors down to 0.5%, 99p latency back to SLO for canary pool. promoting changes region-wide.

sara: immediate customer follow-up: CS to confirm with acme-corp and sentry-proxy. ops to keep watch for 2 hours. open action items for postmortem.

customer-success-jamie: acme-corp acknowledged, wants RCA and assurance on config rollout testing. logged customer concern in CRM.

ops-bot: rate-limit rule applied to heavy route at 09:36 UTC. sample log: `tenant=acme-corp, rejected=4 per minute` — acceptable.

ryan: root cause hypothesis: recent perf tuning increased `max_batch_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` to optimize throughput but didn't account for certain client burst patterns — when many long sequences arrive, batching aggregations cause memory pressure and eviction storm -> paging -> perf cliff.

sara: handoff to evening oncall @liz at 11:00 UTC. please monitor memory, eviction rate, and any queueing metrics. also prioritize a new smoke test that simulates bursty long-sequence clients.

liz: ack. I'll own the night handoff, and I'll coordinate an engineering follow-up: add canary validation to runtime-config changes and a gating test for cont-batch changes.

oncall-miguel: postmortem owners: ryan + liz + infra-eli. tentative timeline: hotfix timeline + impact + mitigation steps. I'll write the initial incident timeline and open INC-2026-0315-001-postmortem.

sara: final note — temporary change diff saved: `cont_batch: {max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 1024, max_num_seqs: 32 -> 6, batch_timeout_ms: 200 -> 100}`. we should consider introducing adaptive limits and per-tenant backpressure to avoid global storms.

dev-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2 at 10:05 UTC. last_message_ts updated.

oncall-miguel: last checks at 10:10 UTC look stable. handing off to liz at 11:00 UTC. closing active incident channel threads and attaching logs to the postmortem.
